[Messages]
[systems]: This case concerns a dispute under a multi-year supply agreement between Alpha Components (supplier) and Northbridge Medical Systems (buyer). The disputed issues include: (1) whether Northbridge breached a volume commitment clause by reducing orders in the last two quarters; (2) whether Alpha failed to meet agreed delivery schedules and quality specifications during the same period; and (3) what payment, credit, or adjustment is owed as a result. Please review the parties' initial statements below.

[SupplierRepresentative]: We appreciate the chance to present Alpha Components' position, but we must be clear that Northbridge's current stance is, in our view, commercially unreasonable.

Alpha entered into a three-year supply agreement with Northbridge on 1 March 2023 for custom controller boards. The pricing and capital investments on our side were explicitly premised on a minimum annual volume commitment of 24,000 units. The contract language in Section 4.2 (Volume Commitment and Shortfall Payments) is straightforward and does not make the commitment optional or purely aspirational.

From March 2023 through January 2024, Northbridge's purchase orders tracked this commitment. Then, without invoking any contractual excuse, they abruptly slashed orders to 800 units in February, 600 in March, and 500 in April. They did this while we were carrying inventory and capacity tailored to their forecast. We attach a detailed PO and delivery history showing compliance on our side.

Northbridge now refuses to pay the shortfall invoice of $1.05M that we issued in accordance with the contract. Instead, they point to a handful of delivery slippages and quality issues which, while unfortunate, were limited, promptly remedied, and squarely within the agreed cure mechanisms. On-time performance remained above 96%, and only 73 units out of more than 20,000 delivered required rework, all handled at our expense within the agreed timelines.

To use these isolated issues as a pretext to walk away from a clear volume commitment and leave us with $1.4M in stranded inventory and dedicated capacity is not consistent with the deal we struck. We therefore ask the platform to confirm that Northbridge is obligated to pay the $1.05M shortfall and either (a) resume ordering at the contracted minimum volumes, or (b) pay the early-termination fee under Section 9.3. Anything less effectively rewards them for unilaterally rewriting the bargain after we made substantial investments.

[BuyerRepresentative]: Northbridge respectfully submits that Alpha's portrayal of events is incomplete and their demand is excessive and unacceptable as framed.

It is true that the written agreement contains a volume commitment. However, Alpha omits the equally important provisions tying our obligations to their consistent ability to meet delivery schedules and quality requirements, which are critical for a regulated medical-device manufacturer.

Starting in November 2023, we faced repeated delays. For example, PO #NB-231108 (2,400 units requested for delivery by 15 December 2023) arrived in three batches, with the last 600 units not arriving until 12 January 2024. Comparable delays affected PO #NB-240102 and PO #NB-240215. We attach our internal incident log, which documents these slippages and the resulting disruption to our own production.

At the same time, we observed a non-trivial rise in quality issues. While Alpha did take corrective action, the cumulative effect was that we could no longer reasonably rely on them as a sole-source, just-in-time supplier. Under those circumstances, continuing to order at prior levels would have exposed Northbridge to unacceptable operational and regulatory risks.

Alpha's $1.05M shortfall invoice assumes a rigid, one-sided reading of Section 4.2 and ignores the additional costs and delays we incurred. It effectively requires us to pay full margin on volumes we did not order precisely because of Alpha's performance issues. That is not a balanced or commercially sensible outcome.

We are prepared to pay for all conforming product actually received and to consider a limited accommodation that reflects both parties' contributions to the situation. But we cannot accept Alpha's all-or-nothing claim. We ask the platform to critically examine the delivery and quality record, and to reject the notion that the buyer must bear the entire economic burden despite Alpha's documented shortcomings.
rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Composing a request for documents**

I need to craft a concise communication. It should ask both parties for specific documentation, including contractual excerpts, records, invoices, logs, reports, and communication timelines. I want to keep the tone neutral and professional, so I’ll propose a temporary hold if necessary and request that they provide these documents within a specified timeframe. I’ll also want them to clarify the numerical relief they seek and their willingness to negotiate. I'll summarize the dispute and clearly state our needs.
**Requesting key documents**

I need to ask both parties to submit specific documents. For Alpha, I’ll request contract sections 4.2 and 9.3, as well as the PO/delivery history and shortfall invoice. For Northbridge, the same contract sections must be included, along with the incident log and calculations for damages. I’ll set a deadline for submission, asking them to provide everything within 7 calendar days. I'll also remind them to preserve evidence and quantify the relief sought. This will be done while keeping the tone neutral and professional.
**Requesting document submissions**

I’m going to reach out to Alpha and ask them to upload signed contract pages from Sections 4.2 and 9.3, along with the purchase order and delivery history, the shortfall invoice, inventory or cost backup, and records of their cure attempts with performance metrics. For Northbridge, I’ll request the same contract pages, purchase order receipts, an incident log, and evidence of production disruption, including calculations for damages. I’ll set a deadline of within 7 calendar days in native formats and ask for certification that relevant records won't be destroyed. After reviewing the submissions, I’ll provide a statement of preliminary findings.
rounds.response: I will review the dispute but need full documentation from both parties before making findings. Alpha: upload the executed contract pages showing Sections 4.2 and 9.3, the complete PO and delivery history, the $1.05M shortfall invoice and your shortfall calculation, inventory/cost substantiation for stranded stock and capacity, and records of any cure notices, rework, and on-time-performance metrics. Northbridge: upload the same contract pages, the POs/receipts for disputed shipments, your incident log and nonconformance reports, evidence of production/regulatory impact and alternative sourcing or mitigation steps, and your calculation of offsets/damages. Produce these documents in native format and certify preservation of relevant records within 7 calendar days. After I receive and review the materials I will issue preliminary findings and either convene a settlement conference or provide a final determination.

rounds.consequence: Your structured, neutral request for detailed documentation and preservation of records is logged by the platform as meeting procedural expectations and contributing positively to case organization; both parties respond by complying, though they also use their submissions to reiterate criticisms of each other's positions.

rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Considering settlement options**

I’m thinking about directing both parties to submit proposed settlement calculations and maybe offer mediation or even a settlement conference. It might also make sense to issue preliminary findings suggesting both have some responsibility while justifying why. Considering that neither side provided pre-invoice breach notice, I could instruct them to propose offset calculations and set a deadline for mediation. Ultimately, we'd want a clear, documented resolution that aligns with the platform policies.
**Pursuing resolution steps**

I’m considering asking both parties to submit their proposed calculations for the net amount. Given that I've already requested documents and now have them, it's time to keep moving toward a resolution. I could issue a preliminary determination stating both parties breached contracts. Alpha might owe damages for delivery quality, while Northbridge owes the shortfall minus an offset. To be safer, I could recommend expert assessment and mediation, perhaps appointing a technical auditor to quantify impacts and suggest payments.
**Structuring payment and mediation**

I need to remain impartial and justified in this situation. Considering both sides had issues, proposing an interim split-the-difference approach seems reasonable. I might suggest that Northbridge pays 50% of the shortfall invoice of $525,000 within 10 days, either to escrow or directly to Alpha, while both parties participate in mediation and a technical audit within 21 days. The audit would quantify damages, with final reconciliation in 30 days. If either party fails to cooperate, they would face cost consequences, which should help keep things fair.
**Outlining preliminary findings and orders**

I’m establishing preliminary findings: both parties breached their obligations. Alpha had ongoing delivery and quality issues that disrupted Northbridge, which in turn reduced orders without a formal breach notice, after issuing complaints. I propose that Northbridge should pay Alpha 50% of the $1.05M shortfall invoice—about $525,000—within 10 days as an interim payment. Both parties must also participate in an independent audit within 30 days to gauge damages and necessary offsets, cooperating fully. After the audit, the platform will finalize the payment reconciliations.
**Ensuring compliance and cost allocation**

If either party refuses to comply or withholds cooperation, the platform may view that as adverse and allocate costs accordingly. I need to make sure the tone remains neutral and non-threatening, emphasizing the platform's authority in the situation. Also, succinctness is key, ensuring clarity in the wording. I’m careful with number formatting, especially noting the $525,000 amount. Alright, I think I'm ready to finalize everything neatly!
rounds.response: Preliminary view: the record shows both parties contributed to the breakdown—Alpha had recurring late/partial shipments and quality nonconformances that materially disrupted Northbridge, and Northbridge reduced volumes without issuing a formal breach/termination notice after raising repeated concerns—so neither side fully prevails on the papers. Interim order: Northbridge must pay Alpha 50% of the $1.05M shortfall invoice ($525,000) within 10 calendar days as an interim payment pending final reconciliation. Next step: the parties shall jointly submit names of up to three impartial technical/audit firms within 7 days; the platform will appoint one to quantify delivery/nonconformance impacts, mitigation costs, and the appropriate offset to the shortfall within 30 days, and both parties must cooperate. Final reconciliation: after the audit report the platform will issue a final determination; if the audit reduces Northbridge’s liability Alpha must refund any excess within 10 days, and if it increases liability Northbridge must pay the balance within 10 days. Failure to comply with these orders or to cooperate with the audit may result in adverse cost allocations in the final determination.

rounds.consequence: Your preliminary order requiring a 50% interim payment and mandating an independent technical audit is recorded as a firm exercise of your adjudicative authority. I’ll calculate the net liability by subtracting the offset from the shortfall, considering Northbridge's $525,000 interim payment. Each party's audit fees will be credited, with the liable party covering the total fees.
